items.title: openclaw 2026.11.7
items.bullet_md:
- 🛠 **[openclaw 2026.11.7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.11.7)** — _OpenClaw releases_. — 2026.11.7 makes Gateway restarts resume interrupted replies and child results rather than drop pending work.
  - Automations can repair failures from their owner conversation
  - Recovered or intentionally skipped runs are told apart from genuine failures
  - Browser pairing uses a short code approved on the Gateway host
  - Git and package updates finish through schema changes and busy databases

items.title: Anthropic mathematician claims to have solved prestigious Millennium Prize problem with Claude
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Anthropic mathematician claims to have solved prestigious Millennium Prize problem with Claude](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1010051/anthropic-riemann-hypothesis-millennium-prize-problem)** — _The Verge AI_. — An Anthropic mathematician says Claude helped prove the Riemann hypothesis, the $1 million problem open since 1859.
  - Levent Alpöge published the Lean proof on his own website, not a journal
  - He says the method also resolves the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis
  - Clay's rules require two years of scrutiny before any prize

items.title: Google workers tell their employer not to punish schools that don't want AI
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Google workers tell their employer not to punish schools that don't want AI](https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2026/11/google-alphabet-union-school-ai-protest-gemini-workers-petition/)** — _Hacker News (points)_. — Hundreds of Google staff want their employer to stop tying school Search access to Gemini adoption.
  - The Alphabet Workers Union petition asks Sundar Pichai to retract the policy
  - Schools that switch off Gemini lose Search access starting next year
  - New York City, Los Angeles and Chicago are discussing alternative search engines

items.title: AI coding agents ace isolated tests but complete fewer than one in ten tasks in a simulated workplace
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[AI coding agents ace isolated tests but complete fewer than one in ten tasks in a simulated workplace](https://the-decoder.com/ai-coding-agents-ace-isolated-tests-but-complete-fewer-than-one-in-ten-tasks-in-a-simulated-workplace/)** — _The Decoder_. — Coding agents that ace SWE-bench flunk office life: the best fully completed fewer than one in ten tasks in a 101-task simulation.
  - Claude Opus 5.5 completed 6.93%, GPT-6 Astra 7.92%
  - Agents faced project boards, colleagues and chat histories, not tidy tickets
  - Standard benchmarks like SWE-bench are nearly saturated

items.title: Your AI red team may be finding the same prompt injection thousands of times
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Your AI red team may be finding the same prompt injection thousands of times](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/20/ai-prompt-injection-red-team/)** — _Help Net Security AI_. — A bigger prompt-injection red-team haul can produce a weaker defence, because the extra attacks are often the same trick reworded.
  - PISmith found 7,132 working attacks versus RL-Hammer's 4,282 on 560 tasks
  - Retrained on the bigger pile, Qwen3-4B was hijacked 47.5% of the time, against 27.5%
  - The fix, PIPETTE, rewards unseen techniques and keeps clean-task completion at 64.95%

items.title: Security researchers show how cheap AI inference providers steal keys and snoop on users
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Security researchers show how cheap AI inference providers steal keys and snoop on users](https://the-decoder.com/security-researchers-show-how-cheap-ai-inference-providers-steal-keys-and-snoop-on-users/)** — _The Decoder_. — Cheap inference marketplaces are the weak link: Dragos's canary-token probe caught providers leaking prompts and keys.
  - Dragos sent roughly two million test requests from July through November 2026
  - Attackers harvested hundreds of AWS keys and tested some within hours
  - Zero Data Retention was widely ignored; OpenRouter dropped three providers and 125 endpoints

items.title: Combatting adversarial distillation
items.bullet_md:
- 🟢 **[Combatting adversarial distillation](https://openai.com/index/combatting-adversarial-distillation)** — _OpenAI blog_. — OpenAI says hardened GPT-6.2 Astra defenses cut protected-reasoning extraction from 54% to 0.2% attack success.
  - Adaptive red-teaming on earlier-turn reasoning fell from 54.0% to 0.2%
  - Input and output classifiers now scan tool-call arguments, not just replies
  - Reasoning is tied to its conversation history, so a rewritten message drops what follows
  - Weekly enforcement against distillers runs from thousands to tens of thousands of accounts

items.title: How OpenAI’s Performance Factory keeps ChatGPT fast
items.bullet_md:
- 🟢 **[How OpenAI’s Performance Factory keeps ChatGPT fast](https://openai.com/index/how-openai-performance-factory-keeps-chatgpt-fast)** — _OpenAI blog_. — OpenAI now has Codex agents chase ChatGPT slowdowns end to end, from root cause to a fix PR to post-deploy checks.
  - The Regression Workflow logged 1,700+ investigations and root caused 600+ cases in three months
  - A separate Codex session tries to disprove each diagnosis before a fix is built
  - In a 100-case manual review, 70% of root-cause suggestions were graded accurate
  - Engineers still review and merge every proposed fix

items.title: Signal is blocking Gemini and Siri AI from reading your screen
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Signal is blocking Gemini and Siri AI from reading your screen](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1038390/signal-blocking-ai-agent-screenshots-mobile-app)** — _The Verge AI_. — Signal now blocks screenshots on Android and iOS to keep Siri and Gemini out of your chats, a fix it calls incomplete.
  - Users can re-enable screenshots, at the cost of Signal's privacy guarantees
  - Whittaker says the block misses file-system access and cannot be done on macOS
  - Signal wants Apple, Google and Microsoft to give developers agent-access controls

items.title: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update](https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11/20/1149399/the-most-misunderstood-graph-in-ai-just-got-a-major-update/)** — _MIT Tech Review AI_. — METR's much-misread time-horizon graph now includes fuzzier work, and models fell short of humans there.
  - Not one AI-designed evaluation was good enough for METR staff to use
  - Models also trailed humans at scoring philosophical arguments
  - Opus 5.5 now lands borderline above the bar; a year ago everything was clearly below

items.title: European Commission confirms AI-generated cyberattack disrupted its systems
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[European Commission confirms AI-generated cyberattack disrupted its systems](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/20/european-commission-ai-generated-cyberattack-publicly-available-tool/)** — _Help Net Security AI_. — Hackers used an AI tool to breach the European Commission, forcing apps offline for over 10 days.
  - Detected Oct 22, confirmed Oct 26; no evidence of a staff-wide data breach
  - Sysper HR, MyPMO and translation systems were among those hit
  - CERT-EU had warned two weeks earlier about Artex, an AI pentesting framework

items.title: Introducing harness adapters: adapt your favorite model to your harness to improve performance and cost
items.bullet_md:
- 🟡 **[Introducing harness adapters: adapt your favorite model to your harness to improve performance and cost](https://huggingface.co/blog/harness-adapters-at-scale)** — _Hugging Face blog_. — Hugging Face argues the model-plus-harness pairing, not the model alone, is where performance is being left on the table.
  - Qwen3.8-27B on the pi harness scores 39% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 at 2.9K tokens per task
  - An RL-trained adapter drops average usage to 1.5K tokens per task
  - Gains come from less reasoning, better first attempts and fewer stray tool calls

items.title: Inkling-2-Mini in 5.4 GB Memory
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Inkling-2-Mini in 5.4 GB Memory](https://github.com/ShinMegamiBoson/lookatmyquant)** — _Hacker News (points)_. — A third-party quantiser squeezed Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini into a 5.4 GB build.
  - LookAtMyQuant is MIT-licensed and gives more bits to the parts that matter most
  - The small build beats a larger Unsloth version on GSM8K and HumanEval
  - Runs on an Apple M5 Max, even though the vendor suggests about 20 GB

items.title: Qwen4 Max is live on Together AI
items.bullet_md:
- 🟡 **[Qwen4 Max is live on Together AI](https://www.together.ai/blog/qwen4-max)** — _Together AI blog_. — Together put Alibaba's 2.4-trillion-parameter Qwen4 Max on serverless inference with a 1M-token window, 30% off until Nov 22.
  - Its first test: 344 Tornado files, 652,519 tokens, one patch that passed the maintainers' tests
  - The request cost 69 cents; a cached repeat ran about 3 cents
  - Streaming is mandatory and thinking is on by default, billed as output

items.title: Inkling 2 Mini is "Local Opus"?
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Inkling 2 Mini is "Local Opus"?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JFoMJ17MOOA) — **AICodeKing** (8m37s). — A realistic look at running Inkling 2 Mini locally on a 32 GB Mac, and which jobs to hand it. - Four-bit GGUF weighs 17.6 GB; all 19 OpenRouter test requests cost about 3 cents - Low effort fixed the cache bug in 4 seconds, high effort in 15.4 seconds - Its rate limiter let 1 of 16 requests through; the regex inspector passed 11 of 11

items.title: Black Hat USA 2026 | Trusted Enough to Run: Breaking AI Agents in Official Workflows
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Black Hat USA 2026 | Trusted Enough to Run: Breaking AI Agents in Official Workflows](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T2nC96cVpwQ) — **Black Hat** (35m20s). — Audit method for agent workflows: find where a product marks state safe, then trace where that state is consumed later. - Claude Code's shipped default approval rule still allows arbitrary shell execution - Gemini CLI sanitization fails at runtime, leaving secrets reachable - Codex loads attacker-written workflow state as trusted instructions, making influence persist

items.title: Build the Workshop Before the Software Factory — Armin Ronacher, Earendil
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Build the Workshop Before the Software Factory — Armin Ronacher, Earendil](https://youtube.com/watch?v=JNexz3Tbiu8) — **AI Engineer** (19m56s). — Human attention, not model capability, is the limit: build the workshop before the software factory. - Pi's core tools are unchanged after a year; the models got better - Tasks now run 14 minutes instead of two and a half - 141 projects started, only 10 to 15 kept alive - Executive summaries instead of reading code

items.title: Build Your Own MCP Server in Python, Step by Step
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Build Your Own MCP Server in Python, Step by Step](https://youtube.com/watch?v=tF_rY_cb7Bg) — **aie works: AI How-To** (5m28s). — A 40-line notes server that runs unchanged on both a free local Ollama model and Claude Code. - Built on Python 3.12 with MCP Python SDK 2.3.0 - Tested with Ollama 0.40 running qwen3.5:4b, and Claude Code 2.1.296 - Breaks the tool on purpose, then fixes the useless error with ToolError

items.title: This Opensource Repo Actually saves upto 98% USAGE across Codex,Claude & More!?
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [This Opensource Repo Actually saves upto 98% USAGE across Codex,Claude & More!?](https://youtube.com/watch?v=aFmu4rLgH8U) — **AICodeKing** (8m46s). — Worth trying only if your agent sits on Gemini 4 or an original Fable 5 model. - MIT-licensed, around 7,600 stars; renders bulky context as 5x8 pixel PNG pages - 48,000 characters of prompt and tool docs fall from about 25,000 tokens to 2,700 - Measured 59% to 70% lower end-to-end bill; the Claude Code demo went from $42 to $6 - Sonnet 5.5 read 2 of 15 test hex IDs, so skip imaging it

items.title: AI Writes 44% More Code. So Why Isn't More Software Shipping?
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [AI Writes 44% More Code. So Why Isn't More Software Shipping?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cI1WVdTpFZY) — **DopeShit** (9m12s). — Harvard tracked 720,542 workers at 655 companies: 44% more code written, only ~14% more finished work. - Time to merge rose 56% and review comments rose 39% - Letting AI review the code has not fixed the review line - The same pattern appears in hospitals with AI scribes - Two simulated futures for 2031, and what they mean for developers

items.title: MCP Registry: The App Store for AI Agent Tools
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [MCP Registry: The App Store for AI Agent Tools](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Er0ay2ecHw8) — **Kernel Cast** (2m15s). — For anyone new to MCP: a 2m15s map of the registry agents query to find tool servers. - Entries are `server.json` records pointing at npm, PyPI or OCI packages, or remote URLs - Framed as an App Store for agent tools, spanning GitHub, databases and search

items.title: Google Just Killed the Chatbot Reply (A2UI)
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Google Just Killed the Chatbot Reply (A2UI)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qFAbevIeJN0) — **Better Stack** (8m10s). — For teams wiring agents into product UIs: A2UI 1.0 lets an agent answer with real components instead of text. - JSON cards, forms and buttons render in React, SwiftUI or Android natively - Demo: 170 characters of A2UI Express became almost 6,000 characters of JSON

items.title: Google Gemini 4 Neon Ranks First On The Coding Agent Index With A 58.6 Score
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Google Gemini 4 Neon Ranks First On The Coding Agent Index With A 58.6 Score](https://youtube.com/watch?v=4FmYK2LrN8A) — **AIM Network** (2m45s). — Google tuned this model for software engineering and complex analytical work, and the briefing flags results that vary by test scenario. - 65.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.1 and 46.2% on FrontierCode 2.0 - Benchmark coverage spans multi-step agent runs and standard coding challenges

items.title: 87% of the Anthropic power will come from gas and 11% from coal in 2028
items.bullet_md: - 📰 **[87% of the Anthropic power will come from gas and 11% from coal in 2028](https://betterdatacenterproject.com/2026/11/16/how-ai-is-powered-a-breakdown-of-byop-and-grid-power/)** — _Hacker News (points)_. — A nonprofit's estimate that 87% of Anthropic's 2028 power comes from gas and 11% from coal drew a 920-comment thread on its caveats.

items.title: How Public Evals Work and Fail, and What Should Change
items.bullet_md: - 📝 **[How Public Evals Work and Fail, and What Should Change](https://eugeneyan.com/writing/public-evals)** — _Eugene Yan_. — A teardown of 12 public benchmarks argues the graders, not the models, are now a large share of the failures — eight of twelve showed evidence of failing correct work.

items.title: GnuPG Security Advisory for GPGME
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[GnuPG Security Advisory for GPGME](https://lists.gnupg.org/pipermail/gnupg-announce/2026q4/000517.html)** — _Hacker News (points)_. — GnuPG shipped GPGME 2.3.1 to close a critical double free, CVE-2026-129975.
  - Crafted very long OpenPGP user IDs trigger it; RCE can't be ruled out
  - Everything linked against GPGME before 2.3.0 is affected, including most mail clients
  - Gpg4win 5.1.2 bundles the fix; a patch covers older versions

items.title: If you stop writing code, you also get worse at reviewing it
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[If you stop writing code, you also get worse at reviewing it](https://cekrem.github.io/posts/if-you-stop-writing-code-you-also-get-worse-at-reviewing-it/)** — _Hacker News (points)_. — Christian Ekrem argues that delegating all coding atrophies the review skill, since judging code depends on having written it.
  - Keep practicing, he says; reading AI output is not practice

items.title: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol: The System Card
items.bullet_md:
- 📝 **[GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol: The System Card](https://thezvi.substack.com/p/gpt-62-astra-and-sol-the-system-card)** — _Don't Worry About the Vase (Zvi)_. — Zvi's read of the GPT-6.2 card finds regressions and a model getting harder to monitor, not the needed improvement.
  - Astra is the first externally deployed model to meet OpenAI's High self-improvement threshold
  - Both models hit Critical for cybersecurity; UK AISI still elicited social engineering and fabrication
  - As a monitor it missed 51% of violative transcripts with chain of thought attached

items.title: Policy can still work on short timelines
items.bullet_md: - 📝 **[Policy can still work on short timelines](https://www.transformernews.ai/p/policy-can-still-work-on-short-timelines-california-states-ai)** — _Transformer News_. — Shakeel Hashim argues it is premature to give up on policy, pointing to California's proposed emergency shutdown authority and Trahan's revised FRONTIER ACT as near-term options.

items.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
items.bullet_md:
- 🟢 **[Perplexity and Intelligence](https://openai.com/index/perplexity-and-intelligence)** — _OpenAI blog_. — Jakub Pachocki argues perplexity should be the shared cross-lab yardstick, and proposes common limits labs commit not to cross.
  - OpenAI published numbers on a fixed internal-code set: GPT-3.5 ~0.99, GPT-4 ~0.91
  - Capabilities emerged below 0.8, with math breakthroughs at ~0.76
  - He expects the next transformative window around 0.68-0.7 log-perplexity

items.title: Why data centers are at the center of the Big Tech backlash
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Why data centers are at the center of the Big Tech backlash](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/22/why-data-centers-are-at-the-center-of-the-big-tech-backlash/)** — _TechCrunch AI_. — Paris Marx calls the hyperscale buildout fundamentally unsustainable and completely out of line with a livable planet.
  - Argues data centers are physical, so backlash cuts across the political spectrum
  - Cites Ireland, where data centers use more than 20% of national electricity
  - Says Google once drew 29% of one Oregon city's water

items.title: The Pulse: Is Amazon’s writing culture collapsing because of AI?
items.bullet_md: - 📝 **[The Pulse: Is Amazon’s writing culture collapsing because of AI?](https://newsletter.pragmaticengineer.com/p/the-pulse-is-amazons-writing-culture)** — _Pragmatic Engineer_. — Gergely Orosz asks whether AI is eroding Amazon's writing culture, in an issue also covering Anthropic's largest-ever IPO and Meta's Conductor reversal.

items.title: AltRA-Test: An Alternative Annotator Test for LLM Judges Without Shared Annotators
items.bullet_md:
- 🧪 **[AltRA-Test: An Alternative Annotator Test for LLM Judges Without Shared Annotators](https://huggingface.co/papers/2611.26073)** — _HF Daily Papers_. — A statistical test validates an LLM judge even when no single group of annotators labeled every item.
  - Resamples k human labels per item, swapping one for the LLM annotation
  - LLMs passed in 35.3% of judge-dataset pairs under default CoT, 47.3% at best prompting
  - About 100 items often suffice for a decision

items.title: Fast-Anything: Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow
items.bullet_md:
- 📰 **[Fast-Anything: Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow](https://github.com/EL4CTEO/fast-anything)** — _Hacker News (points)_. — EL4CTEO's fast-anything ports only an app's slowest functions to Rust, then replays recorded calls before enabling each port.
  - port records up to 500 real calls and builds a one-function Rust crate
  - Python fuzzy dedupe went from 4.91s to 42ms, 116x faster

items.title: OpenAI ships GPT-Live-1.1 to API with standby mode cutting idle costs 60%
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[OpenAI ships GPT-Live-1.1 to API with standby mode cutting idle costs 60%](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-live-1.1)** — _AlphaSignal · Nov 20_. — GPT-Live-1.1, OpenAI's full-duplex voice model, is now in the API as gpt-live-1.1 with an optional standby mode.
  - Idle time bills at $0.02 per minute versus $0.05 for active inference
  - Standby timeouts are configurable between 5 and 60 seconds
  - The WebRTC call stays open and resumes when speech returns
  - Ships 38 voice IDs, seven of them new

items.title: Tufa Labs shrinks 1 GB of Wikipedia to 105 MB using only a neural network
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[Tufa Labs shrinks 1 GB of Wikipedia to 105 MB using only a neural network](https://github.com/Tufalabs/tufazip)** — _AlphaSignal · Nov 20_. — Total is 105,388,353 bytes including the decoder archive, roughly a 9.5-fold cut, at about 7.5 days each way.
  - A 163M-parameter transformer is the only predictor, no hand-engineered model
  - Needs exactly two Nvidia B200 GPUs plus CUDA 13.0
  - Decoder archive adds 4.4 MB on top of roughly 101 MB of text
  - MIT-licensed decoder code is on GitHub

items.title: MIT researcher builds a real-time tool to steer LLM output as you write
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[MIT researcher builds a real-time tool to steer LLM output as you write](https://github.com/chuanqisun/spaceship)** — _AlphaSignal · Nov 19_. — An MIT Media Lab researcher open-sourced a browser demo that steers LLM prose while you write.

items.title: Marvell and Penguin's photonic memory appliance pools 16 TB of DDR5 and 1 TB of HBM across 16 servers over optical…
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[Marvell and Penguin's photonic memory appliance pools 16 TB of DDR5 and 1 TB of HBM across 16 servers over optical…](https://www.theregister.com/systems/2026/11/16/marvell-and-penguin-solutions-aim-to-end-the-rampocalypse-with-photonic-memory-fabric/5309921)** — _TLDR · Nov 18_. — Marvell and Penguin pool 16 TB of DDR5 and 1 TB of HBM per appliance, shared by up to 16 servers.

items.title: Google Cloud releases multi-agent tool that writes full research papers from raw notes
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[Google Cloud releases multi-agent tool that writes full research papers from raw notes](https://github.com/google-research/paper-orchestra)** — _AlphaSignal · Nov 18_. — PaperOrchestra is an open-source multi-agent pipeline that turns raw ideas and experiment notes into a submission-ready LaTeX manuscript.
  - Five agents handle outline, literature review, drafting, refinement and plots
  - Plotting is off by default and the benchmark dataset is not included yet
  - Needs Python 3.11, a paper_orchestra Conda env and Gemini or OpenAI API keys

items.title: Rethinking Table File Paths with Uber: Lance's Multi-Base Layout (10 minute read)
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[Rethinking Table File Paths with Uber: Lance's Multi-Base Layout (10 minute read)](https://www.lancedb.com/blog/rethinking-table-file-paths-lance-multi-base-layout)** — _TLDR · Nov 19_. — Lance added a multi-base path layout, built with Uber, that keeps file paths relative across many buckets.
  - Uber spreads one petabyte-scale dataset over N S3 buckets to multiply throughput
  - Writes round-robin across the buckets; reads fan out across all of them in parallel
  - Moving 10 million files across 5 buckets means editing 5 strings, not 10 million paths

items.title: Sashiko: Lessons from building an agentic code review system for Linux (11 minute read)
items.bullet_md:
- 📧 **[Sashiko: Lessons from building an agentic code review system for Linux (11 minute read)](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/application-development/lessons-from-building-sashiko-an-agentic-code-review-system)** — _TLDR · Nov 20_. — Google detailed Sashiko, its open-source Gemini code reviewer for Linux kernel patches.
  - Up to seven specialist sessions run in parallel, each on one bug class
  - About 1,200 reviews a day across more than 100 kernel mailing lists
  - 60-day post-merge fix rate fell to 2.2% in Linux 7.2
  - Sashiko is credited in 2,000+ mainline commits and 528 of 2026's kernel CVEs
